question.text: Consider an engine that absorbs 130 cal of heat from a hot reservoir and delivers 30 cal heat to a cold reservoir in each cycle. The engine also consumes 2 J energy in each cycle to overcome friction. If the engine works at 90 cycles per minute, what will be the maximum power delivered to the load? [Assume the thermal equivalent of heat is $4.2 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{cal}]$

solution.text:
Hint: 
work done per cycle $=100 \times 4.2-2=418 \mathrm{~J}$
Total work done $=418 \times 90$
Power $=\frac{418 \times 90}{60}=627 \mathrm{~W}$
